account:
It is day 1, just after ten, and I have arrived at the mill for my scheduled grain inspection. Several townsfolk are gathered nearby, and the secretary is approaching with a written book. I have not yet heard anything establishing that this gathering is unusual or what it is for beyond ordinary mill business.

The unresolved unusual matter is a vague rumor from Townsfolk 03 concerning a bridge or port change. Yesterday the innkeeper denied proposing or announcing any such change. Builder said the bridge was passable with no confirmed defects, and relayed Freight's account of undamaged roads and an uneventful ferry crossing. I therefore have no evidence of damage or of an actual plan behind the rumor. I want to speak directly with Townsfolk 03, but Neighbour has not found them, and the secretary does not know where they live or work. The conversation remains unconfirmed.

Today I authorized Builder to make a visual survey of the bridge and ferry landings, with two emeralds payable on delivery of written findings. No alterations or repairs are authorized. I separately gave Builder one emerald for a report book and the secretary one for an authorization-record book. This is fact-finding and documentation, not approval for a construction project. The secretary reported no new correspondence this morning. I heard a distant baker's shout while traveling, but could not understand it and cannot infer its meaning. My next business is the mill inspection; later appointments include lunch at home, council letters, tea with Neighbour at three, and afternoon office hours.
